stories.title: Little Rabbit and the Fruit
stories.az: Nağıl: balaca dovşan və rəngli meyvələr
paragraphs: Once upon a time, there is a little rabbit. Little Rabbit is hungry.
Little Rabbit sees a red apple. "Yum!" She sees a yellow banana. "Yum, yum!" She sees green grapes. "Yum, yum, yum!"
She sees a duck. "I am hungry too," says the duck. "Here is a banana for you," says Little Rabbit.
The duck is happy. Little Rabbit eats the red apple. Now she is happy too!

questions.question: Who is the story about?
questions.explain: Nağıl balaca dovşan haqqındadır: "there is a little rabbit".

questions.question: What colour is the apple?
questions.explain: Mətndə deyilir: "a red apple" – qırmızı alma.

questions.question: Who gets the banana?
questions.explain: Dovşan bananı ördəyə verir: "Here is a banana for you".

questions.question: Little Rabbit sees green grapes. Show me the grapes.
questions.say: Little Rabbit sees green grapes. Show me the grapes.
questions.explain: "Grapes" – üzüm deməkdir.

stories.title: Grandma's Magic Box
paragraphs: Once upon a time, Grandma has a magic box. "Open it!" says Grandma. The girl opens the box.
Look! One train! Choo, choo! Two cars! Beep, beep! Three planes! Zoom, zoom!
The baby claps. Clap, clap! The boy laughs. Ha, ha! The girl smiles. "Thank you, Grandma!"
Grandma closes the magic box. "See you tomorrow!"

questions.question: Who has the magic box?
questions.explain: "Grandma has a magic box" – sehirli qutu nənənindir.

questions.question: How many cars are in the box?
questions.say: How many cars are in the box?
questions.explain: Mətndə deyilir: "Two cars! Beep, beep!" – iki maşın.

questions.question: Choo, choo! Show me the train.
questions.say: Choo, choo! Show me the train.
questions.explain: "Choo, choo" qatarın səsidir: "One train! Choo, choo!"

questions.question: Who claps? Clap, clap!
questions.explain: "The baby claps" – körpə əl çalır.

stories.title: The Cold Little Frog
paragraphs: It is winter. It is cold and snowy today. A little green frog sits by the river. "I am cold!" says the frog.
A bird flies to the frog. "Here is my red hat," says the bird. Now the frog has got a red hat.
A cat walks to the frog. "Here is my blue scarf," says the cat. Now the frog has got a red hat and a blue scarf.
A sheep comes too. "Here are my yellow socks," says the sheep. One, two, three, four yellow socks!
Now the frog is warm and happy. "Thank you, my friends!"

questions.question: What is the story about?
options: A frog who swims in a hot river
A cold frog and his kind friends
A bird who loses her hat
A cat who likes snow
questions.explain: Qurbağa üşüyür, dostları ona paltar verir.

questions.question: What does the cat give the frog?
options: A red hat
Yellow socks
A blue scarf
A green coat
questions.explain: "Here is my blue scarf," says the cat.

questions.question: How many yellow socks are there?
options: Four
Two
Three
One
questions.explain: "One, two, three, four yellow socks!"

questions.question: "It is cold and snowy today." What is the weather like?
options: It is hot and sunny.
It is warm and windy.
It is rainy.
There is snow and it is cold.
questions.explain: "Snowy" – qarlı, "cold" – soyuq.

stories.title: Where Is My Teddy?
paragraphs: This is Aysel. She is seven. She has got a brown teddy bear. His name is Bobo.
Every morning Aysel puts her books, her pencil and Bobo in her schoolbag. But today, Bobo is not in the bag!
"Mum, where is my teddy?" asks Aysel. Mum looks under the bed. No teddy. Dad looks in the car. No teddy.
Grandma laughs. "Look at your little brother!" Aysel's brother Tural is three. He is on the sofa with Bobo.
"Tural, can I have my teddy, please?" Tural gives Aysel the teddy. Aysel gives Tural a ball. Now they are both happy.

questions.question: What is the problem in the story?
options: Aysel can't find her teddy bear.
Aysel can't find her pencil.
Tural's ball is broken.
Grandma is sad.
questions.explain: Ayselin ayısı çantada yoxdur: "Bobo is not in the bag!"

questions.question: Where does Mum look?
options: In the car
Under the bed
In the schoolbag
On the sofa
questions.explain: "Mum looks under the bed."

questions.question: How old is Tural?
options: Seven
Five
Three
Six
questions.explain: "Aysel's brother Tural is three."

questions.question: In the story, Aysel puts her things in her schoolbag. Which things?
options: Her ball, her car and her teddy
Her hat, her shoes and her teddy
Her pen, her ruler and her ball
Her books, her pencil and her teddy
questions.explain: "Aysel puts her books, her pencil and Bobo in her schoolbag."

stories.title: Hello from Nigar
stories.az: Məktub: yeni şagird özünü təqdim edir
paragraphs: Dear new classmates, hello! My name is Nigar Hasanova and I am ten years old. I am your new classmate. I am from Sheki, but now my family lives in Baku.
We live in a flat on the fifth floor. It has got three bedrooms, a big kitchen and a small balcony. My bedroom is next to the bathroom. There is a desk, a bed and a lot of books in it.
I can speak English and Russian, and I can play the piano. I can swim too, but I can't ride a bike. Can you teach me?
My favourite subject is art. I love drawing animals. I haven't got any friends in Baku yet, so I am a bit nervous. Please say hello to me on Monday!
Best wishes, Nigar.

questions.question: Why does Nigar write this letter?
options: To invite her friends to a party
To tell her new class about herself
To sell her flat in Baku
To thank her piano teacher
questions.explain: Nigar yeni sinif yoldaşlarına özü haqqında yazır: "I am your new classmate."

questions.question: Where is Nigar from?
options: Baku
Gabala
Sheki
Ganja
questions.explain: "I am from Sheki, but now my family lives in Baku."

questions.question: What can't Nigar do?
options: Swim
Play the piano
Speak Russian
Ride a bike
questions.explain: "I can swim too, but I can't ride a bike."

questions.question: What is next to Nigar's bedroom?
options: The bathroom
The kitchen
The balcony
The living room
questions.explain: "My bedroom is next to the bathroom."

questions.question: Nigar says "I am a bit nervous." How does she feel?
options: Very happy and excited
Tired and hungry
A little worried
Angry with her family
questions.explain: "Nervous" – bir az narahat, həyəcanlı deməkdir.

stories.title: A Day in Murad's Life
paragraphs: Murad is twelve and he lives in Gabala. He gets up at seven o'clock every day. He has breakfast with his sister. He usually eats bread, cheese and eggs, but he doesn't drink coffee. He drinks tea.
His school is between the post office and the park, so he walks there. Lessons start at eight thirty.
After school, Murad goes to the library on Mondays and Wednesdays. On Fridays, he plays football in the park with his friends.
In the evening, his mum often sends him to the shop. Today she needs some milk, six eggs and a kilo of apples. "How much is it?" Murad asks. "Nine manat, please," says the shopkeeper.
Murad does his homework after dinner, and he goes to bed at ten o'clock.

questions.question: What is this text mainly about?
options: Murad's holiday in Gabala
Murad's favourite football team
Murad's usual day
Murad's new school in Baku
questions.explain: Mətn Muradın gündəlik həyatını təsvir edir: oyanır, məktəbə gedir, mağazaya gedir.

questions.question: What does Murad drink at breakfast?
options: Tea
Coffee
Milk
Juice
questions.explain: "He doesn't drink coffee. He drinks tea."

questions.question: Where is Murad's school?
options: Next to the library
Between the post office and the park
Opposite the shop
Near the bus station
questions.explain: "His school is between the post office and the park."

questions.question: When does Murad play football?
options: On Mondays
On Wednesdays
Every evening
On Fridays
questions.explain: "On Fridays, he plays football in the park."

questions.question: Murad asks "How much is it?" What does he want to know?
options: The time
The number of eggs
The price
The way to the shop
questions.explain: "How much is it?" – qiyməti soruşmaq üçündür: "Nine manat".

stories.title: A Phone Call in the Kitchen
paragraphs: It is six o'clock on Saturday. Leyla is in the kitchen. Her phone is ringing. It is her friend Aysel.
"Hi, Leyla! What are you doing?" "Hi, Aysel! I'm cooking dinner. I'm making soup and a salad."
"Where is your family?" "My dad is sitting on the sofa in the living room. He is watching football on TV. My little brother is having a shower in the bathroom."
"And your mum?" "She is working today. She is coming home at seven."
"Can I help you? I'm not doing anything." "Yes, please! There aren't any tomatoes in the fridge. Can you bring some?" "Of course. I'm leaving now. See you soon!"

questions.question: What is the phone call mostly about?
options: Leyla's plans for next Saturday
What Leyla and her family are doing now
A football match that Aysel is watching
Shopping for dinner with Leyla's mum
questions.explain: Aysel soruşur: "What are you doing?" Leyla özü, atası, qardaşı və anası indi nə etdiyini danışır.

questions.question: What is Leyla's dad doing?
options: He is watching football on TV.
He is cooking soup.
He is having a shower.
He is working.
questions.explain: "He is watching football on TV."

questions.question: Where is Leyla's little brother?
options: In the kitchen
In the living room
In the garden
In the bathroom
questions.explain: "My little brother is having a shower in the bathroom."

questions.question: What does Aysel bring?
options: Some soup
Some tomatoes
Some milk
A salad
questions.explain: "There aren't any tomatoes in the fridge. Can you bring some?"

questions.question: Leyla says "There aren't any tomatoes in the fridge." What does this mean?
options: The fridge is full of tomatoes.
She doesn't like tomatoes.
There are no tomatoes in the fridge.
The tomatoes are in the bathroom.
questions.explain: "There aren't any" – heç yoxdur deməkdir.

stories.title: A Rainy Holiday in Gabala
paragraphs: Last summer, my family and I went to Gabala for five days. We travelled by car from Baku, and the journey took about four hours. My little brother Tural slept all the way, but I looked out of the window at the green hills and the mountains.

We stayed at a small hotel near the forest. Our room was on the second floor, and it had a big balcony. On the first morning, we took the cable car up the mountain. It was cold at the top, but I was happy because I had my warm jacket.

On the third day, it rained all day, so we didn't go outside. While my parents were reading in the hotel café, Tural and I played board games with two children from Sheki. Their names were Aysel and Kamal, and they were very friendly.
On the last evening, we bought some honey and jam at the market for our grandmother. I didn't want to go home. I hope we can go back to Gabala next year!

questions.question: What is the text mainly about?
options: A school trip to Sheki
A day at the market in Baku
A family holiday in Gabala
A weekend at grandmother's house
questions.explain: Mətn ailənin Qəbələdə keçirdiyi beş günlük tətildən danışır: "my family and I went to Gabala for five days".

questions.question: How did the family travel from Baku to Gabala?
options: By car
By cable car
By bus
By train
questions.explain: "We travelled by car from Baku". Kanat yolu (cable car) ilə isə dağa qalxdılar.

questions.question: What did the children do on the rainy day?
options: They read books in the hotel café.
They played board games with two new friends.
They took the cable car up the mountain.
They went to the market.
questions.explain: "Tural and I played board games with two children from Sheki". Kafedə kitab oxuyanlar valideynlər idi.

questions.question: What did they buy for their grandmother?
options: A warm jacket
Some board games
Some cakes and sweets
Some honey and jam
questions.explain: "we bought some honey and jam at the market for our grandmother".

A kind of car
The time you travel from one place to another
A road in the mountains
questions.explain: "Journey" – bir yerdən başqa yerə səfər, yol. Bakıdan Qəbələyə yol təxminən dörd saat çəkdi.

stories.title: Plans for the Weekend
paragraphs: It is Friday afternoon, and Leyla and Murad are walking home from school.
"What are you going to do this weekend, Murad?" Leyla asks.

"On Saturday morning, I'm playing football with my team. The match starts at ten o'clock. In the afternoon, I'm going to stay at home and practise the guitar. I'm learning a new song. What about you?"
"I'm not sure yet. I usually go swimming on Saturdays, but the pool is closed this week. Maybe I'll do some painting. I love drawing pictures of animals."
"Why don't you come to the match? After that, we can go to the park and take some photos. You're really good at photography!"
"That's a great idea! I'll bring my camera. But look at those dark clouds. I think it's going to rain tomorrow."
"Don't worry. If it rains, we'll go to the cinema instead. There's a new film about dolphins."
"Perfect! I'll meet you at the stadium at a quarter to ten. See you tomorrow, Murad!"

questions.question: What are Leyla and Murad mainly talking about?
options: A football match they watched last week
Their plans for the weekend
A film about dolphins they saw
Their new photography club
questions.explain: Onlar həftəsonu nə edəcəklərini planlaşdırırlar: "What are you going to do this weekend?"

questions.question: Why can't Leyla go swimming this Saturday?
options: She has a football match.
She is learning a new song.
It is going to rain.
The pool is closed this week.
questions.explain: "I usually go swimming on Saturdays, but the pool is closed this week."

questions.question: What time will Leyla meet Murad at the stadium?
options: At a quarter to ten
At ten o'clock
At a quarter past ten
In the afternoon
questions.explain: "I'll meet you at the stadium at a quarter to ten." Matç isə saat onda başlayır.

Go to the park and take photos
Go to the cinema
Go swimming

Leyla draws good pictures of animals.
Leyla plays football very well.
Leyla has a new camera.
questions.explain: "Good at photography" – fotoşəkil çəkməyi yaxşı bacarmaq deməkdir.

stories.title: The Prince and the Magic Flower
paragraphs: Once upon a time, there was a young prince who lived in a beautiful palace. He was the richest boy in the country, but he was also the unhealthiest. He ate cakes and sweets all day, he never walked anywhere, and he went to bed very late. He often had headaches, and he was always tired.

One day, the king called the wisest doctor in the land. The old woman looked at the prince and said, "There is a magic flower at the top of the hill. If you walk there every morning, you will find it and feel better. But you must go on foot, and you shouldn't eat sweets before you go."

The next morning, the prince walked up the hill. It was harder than he thought, and he didn't find the flower. He went again the next day, and the next. After a month, he was stronger, faster and happier than before, and he slept much better.
At last, he said to the doctor, "I never found the magic flower, but I feel wonderful!" The doctor smiled. "The walk was the magic," she said.

questions.question: What is the lesson of the story?
options: Magic flowers can cure every illness.
Rich people are always happy.
Kings should listen to their sons.
Walking and healthy habits make you feel better.
questions.explain: Həkimin sözü: "The walk was the magic" – yəni sağlam vərdişlər və gəzinti insanı sağlam edir.

questions.question: What was wrong with the prince at the start of the story?
options: He had a bad cough.
He was always tired and often had headaches.
He was too poor to buy food.
He couldn't walk.
questions.explain: "He often had headaches, and he was always tired."

questions.question: What did the doctor tell the prince to do?
options: Walk up the hill every morning
Eat the magic flower
Ride a horse to the top of the hill
Sleep in the afternoon
questions.explain: "If you walk there every morning, you will find it and feel better. But you must go on foot".

questions.question: How was the prince different after a month?
options: He was richer and more famous.
He was taller than the king.
He was stronger, faster and happier.
He was older and wiser than the doctor.
questions.explain: "After a month, he was stronger, faster and happier than before".

questions.question: "The king called the wisest doctor in the land." "The wisest" means the doctor who…
options: was the oldest of all
knew the most and gave the best advice
was the richest of all
walked the fastest
questions.explain: "Wise" – müdrik, ağıllı; "the wisest" – ən müdrik. Həkimin məsləhəti həqiqətən ağıllı idi.

stories.title: Green City: A School That Recycles
stories.az: Radio müsahibəsi: məktəbdə təkrar emal layihəsi
paragraphs: Good morning and welcome to Green City, the programme about people who are changing Baku for the better. My guest today is Aysel Karimova, a science teacher who has started a recycling project at her school. Good morning, Aysel.
Good morning, and thank you for inviting me.
So, how long have you worked on this project?

We started it two years ago. At that time, our school threw away thousands of plastic bottles every month, and nobody had really thought about it. Then a student called Tural asked me why we didn't recycle them. I didn't have a good answer, so we decided to do something.
And what have you done since then?

Quite a lot! We've put recycling bins in every corridor, and the students have collected more than fifty thousand bottles. A local company has turned them into benches for the school garden. We've also planted two hundred trees around the playground.
That's really impressive. Have you had any problems?
Of course. At first, some students weren't interested, and the bins were often full of food. But we've organised competitions between classes, and now everyone wants to win.
What's next for the project?
We haven't finished yet. Next year, we want to put solar panels on the roof, so the school can use clean energy from the sun.
Aysel Karimova, thank you so much, and good luck!

options: How to become a science teacher
A school recycling project and what it has achieved
A company that makes garden benches
Putting solar panels on houses in Baku

stories.title: The Stranger on the Train
paragraphs: Last winter, Nigar was travelling by train from Baku to Sheki to visit her grandmother, who lived alone in an old house near the mountains. It was snowing heavily, and the carriage was almost empty. Opposite her sat an old man whose coat was still wet from the snow. He was holding a small wooden box which looked very old.

While the train was crossing a bridge, it suddenly stopped, and the box fell to the floor. A gold watch rolled under Nigar's seat. She picked it up and read the words on the back: "To Kamal, with love."

The old man thanked her and smiled. He explained that his wife had given him the watch on their wedding day. Soon after that, he had found a job in another country, where he had worked for more than thirty years. He had sent letters and money home every month, but he hadn't been back for a very long time. "Now I've retired," he said, "and I'm going home to the town where I was born."

When the train arrived in Sheki, Nigar's grandmother was waiting on the platform. Nigar waved to her, but to her surprise, her grandmother ran straight past her and hugged the old man. "Kamal, you're home at last!" she cried.
Nigar couldn't believe it. The kind stranger whom she had helped on the train was her own grandfather, whom she had never met. Her grandmother had wanted it to be a surprise.

questions.question: What is the surprise at the end of the story?
options: The gold watch belonged to Nigar.
Nigar's grandmother was not at the station.
The old man was Nigar's grandfather.
The train never arrived in Sheki.
questions.explain: "The kind stranger whom she had helped on the train was her own grandfather".

The old man fell asleep.

Someone opened the window.

Nigar's mother
A stranger on a train
His wife, on their wedding day

He had worked in another country for many years.
He had been ill in hospital.
He and her grandmother had stopped writing letters.

questions.question: "Now I've retired," he said. What does "retired" mean?
options: Found a new job
Become very tired
Stopped working because of age
Lost something important
questions.explain: "Retire" – təqaüdə çıxmaq, yaşa görə işi dayandırmaq. Buna görə o, evə qayıdır.

stories.title: How to Find Your First Job
stories.az: Çıxış: ilk iş tapmaq üçün məsləhətlər
paragraphs: Good afternoon, everyone. My name is Leyla Hasanova, and I work as a manager at a technology company in Baku. Thank you for inviting me to talk about finding your first job. When I finished university, I had no idea what to do, so today I'd like to share some advice that helped me a lot.

First, think about what you enjoy doing. If you love working with people, a job where you sit alone at a computer all day probably won't make you happy. If you're good at solving problems, you might enjoy working in engineering. Don't choose a career just because it pays well.

Second, start getting experience now. Many companies offer summer internships for students. If I were you, I would apply for two or three, even if they are unpaid. Volunteering is also useful, because it shows employers that you are responsible and keen to learn.

Third, prepare carefully for interviews. Before going to an interview, find out about the company and practise answering common questions with a friend. Remember to arrive on time, and avoid looking at your phone. At the end, it's a good idea to ask one or two questions about the job, because this shows that you are really interested.
Finally, don't be afraid of making mistakes. I failed my first three interviews, but each time I learned something new. If you keep trying, you will find the right job. Good luck!

options: Managers who interview new workers
Young people who are looking for their first job
Engineers who want a better salary
Company owners who need volunteers
questions.explain: Leyla ilk iş axtaran gənclərə məsləhət verir: "talk about finding your first job".

really wanting to learn
too busy to learn
already good at everything
questions.explain: "Keen to" – nəyisə həvəslə etmək istəmək. Yəni öyrənməyə çox həvəslisən.

stories.title: The Stolen Bracelet Comes Home
stories.az: Xəbər reportajı: muzeydən oğurlanan bilərzik tapıldı
paragraphs: Good evening. A gold bracelet which was stolen from the Sheki History Museum last month has been found, and two men have been arrested in connection with the theft. The bracelet, which is believed to be more than eight hundred years old, was handed back to the museum this morning.

The theft was discovered on a Monday morning, when a cleaner noticed that a glass case in the main hall had been opened. At first, police thought the thief must have broken in through a window, but no damage was found anywhere in the building. "Whoever did this can't have forced their way in," one detective told reporters at the time. "They must have had a key, or someone must have let them in."

That detective turned out to be right. Security cameras showed that a man had been allowed into the building by a night guard shortly after midnight. The guard, who had worked at the museum for only three weeks, was questioned and later admitted that he had been offered money to switch off the alarm. Information he gave led officers to a flat in Baku, where the bracelet was found hidden inside a box of old books.

Both men have been charged with burglary and are expected to appear in court next month. If they are found guilty, they could face up to seven years in prison. The museum's director, Mrs Aliyeva, said she was relieved. "We were afraid it might have been sold abroad and that we would never see it again," she explained. "It has been an extremely difficult few weeks for our staff."

Security at the museum is now being reviewed, and new cameras will be installed before the end of the year. The bracelet will be put back on display on Saturday, when entry to the museum will be free for all visitors.

questions.question: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A museum that is opening a new main hall
How a stolen museum object was recovered and the suspects were caught
A night guard who bravely stopped a robbery

questions.explain: Reportaj oğurlanmış bilərziyin tapılmasından və iki nəfərin həbsindən bəhs edir: "has been found, and two men have been arrested".

questions.question: What can we conclude about the night guard?
options: He had worked at the museum for many years
He was the one who found the bracelet in Baku
He refused the money he was offered

stories.title: A Month Without Social Media
stories.az: Podkast: sosial şəbəkəsiz bir ay və peşmanlıqlar
paragraphs: Hi everyone, and welcome back to Screen Time, the podcast where we talk honestly about life online. I'm Aysel, and today I want to tell you about something a bit personal. Last spring, I decided to give up social media for a whole month.

To be honest, I had been putting it off for ages. I used to wake up and check my phone before I even got out of bed. I would scroll through endless posts, watch videos that had gone viral, and compare my ordinary life with the perfect photos of people I had never met. I knew that a lot of what I saw was fake or sponsored, but I kept going back for more.

Things came to a head when I missed my best friend's birthday dinner. I hadn't forgotten it exactly. I had simply lost track of time while I was reading comments under a news story that turned out to be completely false. If I had put my phone away that evening, I wouldn't have let her down. I still wish I had been there.

So I deleted the apps. The first week was tough. I kept reaching for my phone without thinking, and I worried that I was missing out on something important. But slowly, I started picking up old habits. I read three novels, I took up running again, and I actually called people instead of just liking their posts.

Now, I'm not saying social media is evil. It helps small businesses, and it gives ordinary people a voice. I'm back online now, but I've cut down to thirty minutes a day. Sometimes I wish I could switch it off completely, but I've realised the real problem wasn't the apps. It was me not setting any limits. So here's my question for you this week. If you could change one online habit, what would it be?

questions.question: What is Aysel's main point in this episode?
options: Social media should be banned for young people
Fake news is the biggest danger online
She regrets ever creating social media accounts
The real problem was her lack of limits, not the apps themselves
questions.explain: Sonda deyir: "the real problem wasn't the apps. It was me not setting any limits."

questions.question: What finally made Aysel decide to take a break?
options: She missed her best friend's birthday dinner
She read a false news story about her friend
Her phone stopped working one morning
A video she posted went viral
questions.explain: "Things came to a head when I missed my best friend's birthday dinner."

questions.question: "I had been putting it off for ages." What does "putting it off" mean?
options: Talking about it
Delaying it
Enjoying it
Hiding it
questions.explain: "Put off" – təxirə salmaq. Aysel bu qərarı çoxdan təxirə salırdı.

questions.question: How does Aysel use social media now?
options: She has deleted all the apps for good
She only uses it for her small business
She spends about thirty minutes a day on it
She checks it before she gets out of bed
questions.explain: "I'm back online now, but I've cut down to thirty minutes a day."

questions.question: How does Aysel feel now about the evening of the birthday dinner?
options: She thinks her friend overreacted
She still regrets not being there
She is glad she read the comments
She has completely forgotten about it
questions.explain: "I still wish I had been there" – o hələ də peşmandır ki, dostunu məyus edib.

stories.title: Music, Memory and Choice
stories.az: Universitet mühazirəsi: musiqi, yaddaş və seçim
paragraphs: Good morning, everyone. Today I'd like to turn to a study which has attracted considerable attention in recent months, partly because its findings run counter to what many of us had assumed. The research was carried out over a period of two years by a team at a university in Baku, and it set out to examine whether listening to music while studying affects how much students remember.

Now, previous studies had produced conflicting results. Some suggested that music aids concentration, while others claimed it was a major distraction. What this team did differently was to give a large sample of over six hundred students a genuine choice. Half of them were allowed to select their own music, or no music at all, while the other half were assigned music by the researchers. Both groups then sat exactly the same memory tests.

What emerged from the data was striking. It was not the type of music that made the most significant difference, nor even whether there was any music at all. It was the element of choice. Students who had chosen their own conditions consistently outperformed those who had not, by an average of around twelve percent. Interestingly, many of the highest scores came from students who had chosen silence.

The researchers argue that having control over one's environment may reduce stress and, in turn, improve focus. However, they are careful not to overstate their case. The study relied heavily on short tests, and it remains unclear whether the effect would hold over a full academic year. There is, in other words, insufficient evidence to draw firm conclusions about long-term learning.

Nevertheless, the findings do raise important questions for teachers and parents. All too often, we impose a single set of rules on every learner. What this study suggests is that giving students a degree of freedom, within reasonable limits, could be just as valuable as any particular technique. Next week, we'll look at the methods section in more detail, so please read the full paper beforehand.

questions.question: What was the main finding of the study described in the lecture?
options: Classical music improves memory more than other types
Being able to choose study conditions mattered more than the music itself
Studying in silence is always the best option
Music is a major distraction for most students
questions.explain: "It was not the type of music that made the most significant difference... It was the element of choice."

questions.question: In what way was this study different from earlier ones?
options: It gave students a genuine choice about their conditions
It lasted for a full academic year
It used long exams instead of short tests
It only studied students who preferred silence
questions.explain: "What this team did differently was to give a large sample of over six hundred students a genuine choice."

questions.question: What does the lecturer say about the highest scores?
options: They all came from students who were assigned music
They were about twelve percent lower than expected
Many of them came from students who had chosen silence
They were achieved only at the end of the two years
questions.explain: "Interestingly, many of the highest scores came from students who had chosen silence."

questions.question: What is the lecturer's attitude towards the study?
options: Dismissive, because the sample was too small
Convinced that schools must change all their rules at once
Uninterested, mentioning it only briefly
Positive about its value but aware of the limits of its conclusions
questions.explain: Mühazirəçi tədqiqatın "important questions" doğurduğunu deyir, lakin "insufficient evidence to draw firm conclusions" olduğunu da vurğulayır – yəni maraqlıdır, amma ehtiyatlıdır.

questions.question: "They are careful not to overstate their case." This means the researchers
options: avoid repeating their results too often
avoid claiming more than their evidence shows
refuse to explain how the study was done
try not to criticise earlier studies
questions.explain: "Overstate" – şişirtmək. Tədqiqatçılar sübutların göstərdiyindən artıq iddia etməkdən çəkinirlər.

stories.title: The Call That Changed Everything
paragraphs: Ten years ago, I was what most people would call a success. Having graduated near the top of my class, I had landed a well-paid job at a large bank in Baku, and on paper, everything was going swimmingly. I was working all hours, burning the midnight oil several nights a week, and telling myself it would all be worth it in the long run.

Little did I know that my whole career was about to be turned upside down. One winter evening, sitting in an empty office long after everyone else had gone home, I received a call from my grandfather in Sheki. He had fallen ill, he said, and could no longer run the small woodworking workshop he had kept going for forty years. Would I come and help him for a few weeks? Not once had I imagined leaving the bank, yet I heard myself saying yes.

Those few weeks changed everything. Working beside him, covered in sawdust, I felt calmer than I had in years. My grandfather was a man of few words, but he never cut corners, and he took enormous pride in every chair and table he made. Watching him, I began to understand that I had been chasing money and status rather than doing something I genuinely cared about.

Of course, leaving the bank was no piece of cake. My parents thought I had lost my mind, and money was tight for the first couple of years. There were moments when I was on the point of giving up and going back. Only when my first big order arrived, from a hotel in Gabala, did I finally feel that I had made the right call.

Today, the workshop employs six people, and my grandfather, now fully recovered, still drops by most mornings to check that we are all pulling our weight. I'm not saying everyone should quit their job tomorrow. But had I not answered the phone that night, I would probably still be sitting in that office, wondering what else life might have offered. Sometimes, the turning point you need arrives disguised as a problem.
